concepts.why: The presence of bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses, mild lymphocytopenia, moderate anemia, and a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells are consistent with lymphoma.

The presence of bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses, elevated creatine kinase, elevated aldolase, and elevated lactate dehydrogenase, along with a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells, are consistent with sarcoma.
The presence of bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses, intermittent fevers, episodic night sweats, and mild lymphocytopenia are consistent with Castleman disease.

The presence of bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses, elevated creatine kinase, elevated aldolase, and elevated lactate dehydrogenase, along with a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells, are consistent with histiocytosis.

The presence of ill-defined, warm, confluent erythema, edema, and tender induration, along with elevated creatine kinase, elevated aldolase, and elevated lactate dehydrogenase, and a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells, are consistent with inflammatory myofascial disease.

rationales.F09: Mild lymphocytopenia could be indicative of an underlying lymphoproliferative disorder, such as lymphoma.

rationales.F12: The presence of a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells is highly suggestive of a lymphoproliferative disorder, such as lymphoma.
